My ad hoc translation of an interview with Hans-Hermann Hoppe concerning the European Union

Mr. Hoppe, what is your opinion on the current situation in Western Europe, especially in the EU?

All large political parties in Western Europe, no matter what they call themselves and which party program they may have, are following the same fundamental idea of a democratic socialism. They use democratic elections to legitimize the taxation of productive people to benefit unproductive people. They tax people who have earned their income and built their wealth by producing goods and services which were then voluntarily acquired by consumers (and, of course, especially the "rich" among them), and then they distribute their confiscated loot among themselves - to the democratic state which they control or which they hope to control, as well as to their many friends in politics, to their supporters and potential voters.

Of course they don't call this kind of politics by its actual name, which would be: Punishing the productive and rewarding the unproductive. That doesn't sound particularly attractive. Instead, you utilize the widespread feeling of envy and claim that you are merely taxing the few "rich" to support the many "poor". But actually, you just make more and more productive people poor and, at the same time, increase the number of unproductive rich.

And how is the situation in the EU?

If you look at the EU, the situation is even worse. The EU is the first step towards the creation of a European super-state which should then culminate in a world government, dominated by the USA and their central bank, the FED. From the beginning of time - and unlike all the nice-sounding political promises - the EU was never created for the sake of free trade and free competition. To achieve that, you don't need thousands of pages of paper full of mandates and regulations! Rather, the central purpose of the EU - which has always been supported by the USA - was the weakening of Germany, the engine of the European economy. To do that, Germany kept being nagged with historical feelings of guilt, and at the same time, it was under pressure to give up larger and larger parts of its already limited sovereignty to the EU in Brussels. Quite telling: Germany gave up its monetary sovereignty and got rid of its traditionally "hard" currency, the DM, to instead implement a "soft" Euro which is being emitted by the European Central Bank (ECB) which is mostly governed by politically connected central banks from countries with traditionally "soft" currencies.

The EU can be characterized by three main properties. First: Harmonization of all taxation and legislation structures of all participating states to reduce economic competition, especially taxation competition, among the states and thus eliminate the competitiveness of all the states.

Second: To emphasize the economic and moral perversity in each state, i.e. the punishment of the productive and the rewarding of the unproductive, a new layer of international income and wealth redistribution was introduced: You punish the economically more powerful states like Germany and the countries of Northern Europe and reward economically weak states (mostly in Southern Europe) and thus reduce the economic performance of all states.

And third, of steadily increasing importance, especially in the last decade: To break the resistance against the increasing transfer of national sovereignty to Brussels, which exists in more and more countries, the EU has embarked on a crusade to weaken national identities and thus the social and cultural cohesion with the goal of finally eliminating them. The idea of a nation, or different nations and regional identities, is being ridiculed and multi-culturalism is being praised as an unquestionable "good". At the same time, you practice a systematic policy of the euphemistic "non-discrimination" or "affirmative action", according to which all persons or groups, except white heterosexual men and especially married fathers, are considered to be historical "victims" whom the aforementioned "culprit group" needs to compensate using legal privileges or special laws to systematically undermine the natural social order. Normal people are being punished while deviants are rewarded.

So can you claim that the leading politicians of the EU are even worse than the politicians who reign in the national governments?

Yes and no. On one hand, all democratic politicians, with very few exceptions, are morally unfettered demagogues. One of my books is called "Der Wettbewerb der Gauner" [eng. "The Competition of Thugs"] which already hints the truth about democracy and democratic parties. There are few differences among the political elites in Berlin, Paris, Rome, etc. and those in Brussels. In fact, the elites of the EU typically are former politicians with the same mentality as their national counterparts, striving to achieve the luxurious EU wages, privileges, and pensions.

On the other hand, the EU elites are, of course, more evil and more dangerous than their national colleagues because their decisions and regulations always affect a much larger amount of people.

How would you forecast the future of the EU?

The EU and the ECB are moral and economic monsters and go against natural law and economic laws. You cannot continuously punish productivity and success and reward laziness and failure without causing a disaster. The EU will stumble from one economic crisis to the next and finally collapse. The Brexit which we could see is just the first step towards an inevitable process of devolution and political decentralization.

What can ordinary people do in this situation?

First and foremost, people must stop falling for the political phrases of "freedom", "prosperity", "social justice", etc. and start seeing the EU like it is in reality: a group of unapologetic arrogant thugs who empower and enrich themselves at the cost of other productive persons. Secondly, the citizens must develop a clear vision of an alternative to the current mess: Instead of a European super-state or a federation of national states, you should imagine a Europe which consists of thousands of Liechtensteins or Swiss cantons which are interconnected through free trade and compete against each other to deliver attractive conditions for productive people.

Can you compare the situation in the USA with the current situation in Europe?

The difference between the situation in the USA and the one in Western Europe is much smaller than people on both sides commonly imagine. First, the developments in Europe since the Second World War are being closely observed, directed, and influenced by the elites in Washington, be it through threats or bribes. Actually, Europe basically became a US-American outpost, a satellite or vassal. You can arrive to this conclusion by observing the stationed US troops which are spread all over Europe to the Russian border. Another indicator are the permanent pilgrimages of the political elite of Europe and their intellectual bodyguards to Washington - more devout and regular than the pilgrimages of a Muslim to Mecca - to receive the blessing of their lords and masters. Especially the German political elite, whose historical guilt complex has meanwhile grown to a mental illness, is noticeable with its cowardice, devotion, and subservience.

Concerning the inner situation in the USA, both European and Americans are typically wrong. Europeans still regard the USA as a land of freedom, of jagged individualism, and an uninhibited capitalism. The other way around, Americans, if they know or think they know the world outside the USA, often see Europe as a place of uninhibited socialism and collectivism which is very foreign to their "American way of life". Actually, there is close to no difference between the so-called "democratic capitalism" in the USA and the "democratic socialism" of Europe.

America may have always had more vocal supporters of a market-economic capitalism, and the USA are still able to attract the best and smartest of them, and indeed the American tax rate is lower than that of most European states, if not much lower, and even higher than that of Switzerland, which is not a EU member state. And concerning the US-American debt, it is even higher than that of most European states and is roughly at the level of the debt of a state such as a notorious economic "problem child" like Greece. It is also true that, in the USA, you can say almost everything you want to say without having to fear any kind of criminal prosecution whereas the same choice of words can potentially lead you into a European prison. But also: The mental illness of "political correctness" which is currently spreading in the Western world like an epidemic has its beginning in the USA, starting with the so-called "civil rights movement" in the 1960s, and it's the USA where it's had the strangest developments and reached the peaks of absurdity. While you won't immediately land in prison when you say something wrong, you face the same, if not a higher, risk of getting your career destroyed than in a European country.

And concerning the US-American foreign policy: While the political elite of the USA "invited" the third world, much before it was a common practice in Europe, the same elite was simultaneously following an aggressive policy of "marching in" all over the world and creating war in, just in the past few decades, Afghanistan, Pakistan, Iraq, Libya, Syria, Sudan, Somalia and Yemen, causing the deaths of hundreds of thousands of innocent civilians and thus creating an international Islamic terrorism which is mostly financed by Saudi Arabia with which the political elites still have friendly relationships.
